question: Should OpenClaw add a backend-neutral distributed scheduler/job ownership contract in core or plugin APIs, document Redis/BullMQ-style orchestration as an external pattern, or defer the broad job layer until narrower HA/runtime/session trackers settle?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend boundary, config shape, credential model, worker failure semantics, observability surface, and core-versus-plugin ownership are product and architecture choices automation cannot safely make.

options.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
options.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, observability, and security review before backend-specific code lands.

options.title: Document External Pattern
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core single-process for now and document ScalyClaw/BullMQ-style orchestration as an external deployment or plugin pattern.

options.title: Defer To Narrower Trackers
options.body: Let cron HA, external session storage, distributed runtime, and federation issues settle first, then revisit whether a broader distributed worker layer is still needed.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
recommendation.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, observability, and security review before backend-specific code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest live issue signal and the clearest current queue/cron architecture history for this decision.
